# CDC Test Fixtures

Recorded Debezium change event envelopes for `tests/test_cdc_normalizer.py`.

The suite runs entirely from these files. No live Kafka, Debezium or
PostgreSQL connection is used — deliberate, because `ci.yml`'s `postgres:15`
service has no `command:` override and so runs at `wal_level=replica`, which
cannot support logical decoding. A test needing a real CDC connection would
turn `develop` red on the first push.

## Captured from a live connector

| File | Operation | Captured |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_event.json` | `op: "r"` — Debezium's initial snapshot read of seed row 1 | Week 23 |
| `insert.json` | one INSERT against `cdc_demo.orders` | M7W26T1, 3 Nov 2026 |
| `update.json` | one UPDATE setting `status='shipped'` | M7W26T1, 3 Nov 2026 |
| `delete.json` | one DELETE | M7W26T1, 3 Nov 2026 |

All four are full messages — both `schema` and `payload` blocks — from
`subop-postgres-cdc.cdc_demo.orders`, registered from
`services/cdc/debezium_postgres_connector.json`. The verification record,
including every command and its verbatim output, is
`docs/planning/cdc_event_verification.md`.

To recapture, run `infrastructure/scripts/capture_cdc_envelopes.py` against a
running connector. It refuses to write unless every column carries
`__debezium.source.column.type` and `before` is fully populated on UPDATE and
DELETE. Then re-run `derive_cdc_fixtures.py` (below).

### Until M7W26T1, these three files were not captures

`insert.json`, `update.json` and `delete.json` were committed in Week 23 as
hand-reconstructed placeholders, pending a capture that did not land until
Week 26. The placeholders used lowercase type names (`int8`, `varchar`);
real Debezium emits uppercase (`INT8`, `VARCHAR`). Every hand-authored drift
fixture copied that guess.

The suite stayed green against the real captures anyway, because each drift
test asserted only that *some* drift was raised. `EXPECTED_DRIFT` in the test
module now asserts the exact difference.

### What the snapshot and streaming phases disagree on

| Column | `snapshot_event.json` | streaming envelopes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `BIGSERIAL` | `INT8` |

Every other column matches exactly, including case. `BIGSERIAL` is
declaration shorthand for `INT8` plus a sequence default; the normaliser maps
it, and `test_snapshot_then_streaming_does_not_halt` covers the sequence a
live connector produces.

## Derived from the real `insert.json`

Generated by `infrastructure/scripts/derive_cdc_fixtures.py`. Each is the real
INSERT envelope with exactly one documented change applied, so a failure names
the change responsible. **Edit the script, not these files.**

| File | The one change |
|---|---|
| `drift_column_added.json` | `discount NUMERIC(5,2)` appears |
| `drift_column_dropped.json` | `updated_at` disappears |
| `drift_column_renamed.json` | `status` becomes `order_status`, in schema and payload |
| `drift_type_changed.json` | `status` becomes `TEXT` |
| `drift_column_widened.json` | `status` becomes `VARCHAR(64)` |
| `drift_numeric_rescaled.json` | `amount` becomes `NUMERIC(14,4)` |
| `truncate.json` | `op: "t"` — TRUNCATE, which a default publication publishes (`pubtruncate = t`) |
| `ts_ms_source_vs_processing.json` | commit and processing timestamps set years apart |
| `connect_types_only.json` | native types stripped — what the connector emits without propagation |
| `connect_types_only_widened.json` | `drift_column_widened` with native types stripped |

**The schema changes are applied by hand, not captured.** The structure around
them is real; the changed column's parameters are a reasonable model of what
Debezium would emit. `drift_type_changed.json` in particular omits length and
scale for `TEXT`, since Debezium's values for an unconstrained type have not
been observed. M7W27T1's `ALTER TABLE` step produces a real drifted envelope
and is the opportunity to replace one of these with a capture.

`ts_ms_source_vs_processing.json` exists because the negative assertion
"`ts_ms` is not the top-level processing time" is vacuous when the two values
land in the same millisecond, which real envelopes often do.

`test_without_propagation_a_widening_is_invisible` passes *because* no drift
is detected between the two connect-only files. Before M7W26T2 those two files
were byte-identical, so the test compared a file with itself.

Malformed envelopes are parametrised inline in the test module rather than
committed here — they are one-line shapes (a null payload, a string where a
dict belongs) and a file each would obscure more than it documents.
